observations.description: When the original flow is egressing out through an aggregated Ethernet (AE) interface, the corresponding sampled sflow frame does not reflect the correct egress port number. This happens only when the flow is egressing out through an aggregated Ethernet (AE) interface. For non-AE egress interface, this works fine and the sflow frame reflects the correct egress port.
Only on ACX700 devices when the device is rebooted incorrect CT values are seen. Though incorrect CT values are seen, it does not impact any functionality.

On ACX7024 Junos OS Evolved platform, performance measurement impact is seen (measurement is incorrect since compensation removed) on deactivating both chassis and PTP configuration and power off USB. It is very unlikely sequence to be happened.

When ingress policer is configured, to drop ingress traffic, on an interface with upMep the CFM packets generated from the upMep is also dropped due to the policer. This leads to CFM session going down.

When DHCP trace options are enabled, there is a possibility that jdhcpd could generate a core file. In general, traceoptions should be enabled only for debugging. They should be disabled once debugging is done.

This is day-1 issue of Juniper Networks server. It exists on all ACX Series platforms where Juniper Networks server runs. Once the asymmetry configured at slave port, the error propagated to the down stream eventually causes performance issue of spike.

The application rpd-agent might restart with a core file after interface related event changes. This issue is likely to occur when the interfaces are activated/deactivated/created/deleted. This could be due to Bulk change in interface configuration or Admin-initiated application restart through command request system application node re0 restart app <application> System triggered automatic application restart due to internal events. NOTE: This issue occurs due to very rare combination of events and is not seen in most use cases. There is no service impact when the issue occurs, and router operations are unaffected.

When a device is rebooted with PAA installed in 25.2R1, PAA installation on reboot might fail due to Not found default vrf error. This can be resolved by deactivating and activating or freshly installing the PAA configuration.

On all Junos OS Evolved ACX Series platforms, modifying an ECMP route triggers the deletion of the old Next Hop route, which can temporarily disrupt traffic flow until the new route is fully established.
[ACX7000 Series] DHCPv4/v6 packets might be dropped because DHCP packets are not routed to kernel after initial jdhcpd starts.
Traffic is dropped without entering the SRv6 dynamic tunnel.
Packet corruption in L3VPN traffic with preserve-nexthop-hierarchy.
ACX7509: LACP interfaces stuck in Attached state.
High CPU utilization observed on all Junos OS Evolved ACK7000 platforms.
Junos OS Evolved-pfemand process crashes on ACX7348/ACX7332/ACX7024/ACX7509 platforms.
Possible SSD read disturbance due to platform_monitor script accessing the drive every 5 seconds.
PTP packets which are incoming with with padded bytes are dropped on certain Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms.
Default route installation fails on Junos OS Evolved ACX Series platforms.
Traffic statistics are missing for ipdemux lite subscribers for certain Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms.
The Devdb messages are seen continuously on ACX Junos OS Evolved platforms.
Firewall Policer causing unintended packet drops when VRF route leak with static route to next-table is enabled.
The IRB VGA is not shown after deleting one of the IRB interfaces with the same VGA address configured.
The evo-pfemand process crashes on ACX Series platforms without specific trigger.
ACX platform configured as a data center gateway with EVPN-VXLAN failed to forward IP prefix routes for inter-data center communication.
Random evo-pfemand.re.re0 crash is observed during boot up.
BFD single hop session flaps seen after a link down event on Junos OS Evolved ACX platform.
Jflow functionality stops working when configured with sflow.
The firewall filter using next-ip as an action does not forward the packets on Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms if the next-ip is resolved to a static route that points to itself.
The rpd crash due to overlapping flow route updates in a single transaction.
The picd process crashes on Junos OS Evolved ACX7509 platforms during Routing Engine switchover.
Log messages "OOPS: Crossing the LIMIT" are observed on dual Routing Engine platforms. The FEC leak is seen on all ACX Series Junos OS Evolved platforms.
Junos OS Evolved system might fail to response to system commands.
Packet drops are seen due to stale entries in multicast group when HCoS is enabled on ACX7100 platforms.
Packet drops are seen for default route when rpf-check loose mode is configured.
Interface down is observed while configuring 1G speed on ACX7332/ACX7348/ACX7509 platforms.
High memory and CPU usage due to unintended phone-home client activation.
Transient traffic loss during multicast route convergence scenarios.
Traffic disruption is observed when successive switchover is performed having single-hop BFD configured in the dual Routing Engine scenario.
Interfaces with the same outer VLAN ID but different inner vlans or inner-lists/ranges report a commit error.
A traffic outage is seen when disabling and enabling the LACP configuration.
Error message is observed after device is restarted.
When DHCP trace options are enabled, there is a possibility that jdhcpd could core. In general, traceoptions should be enabled only for debugging. They should be disabled once debuffing is done.

On PTX10004, PTX10008, and PTX10016 Junos OS Evolved platforms, !Minor alarm LED on FPM(Front Panel Module) is glowing Yellow, although there is no active alarms/errors shown by show system alarms CLI.
The output display of show ptp global-information has been updated to align the columns and to include only those items that are relevant to the configured profile.

On Junos Evolved PTX platforms, the log message "CFMMAN: Parse Error: CFM CCM pkt TLV parsing error" migiht appear when an FPC or PFE is restarted and comes online. This message indicates that a CFM Continuity Check Message (CCM) was truncated, leading to an error while parsing the TLV (Type-Length-Value) fields in the packet. The error is transient and typically affects only a small number (usually 1 or 2) of CCM packets received immediately after the FPC or PFE becomes operational. It has no functional impact on CFM sessions or overall network operations. CFM continues to function normally, and no persistent degradation is observed. This issue does not consistently affect any specific CFM session and occurs only during the brief initialisation period of the hardware component.
On Junos OS Evolved based platforms, while using ping, traceroute, or other utility that requires host name resolution, an error is raised indicating hostname resolution has failed.

This is a transient log which sometimes is seen when LSI is recreated. This has no functional impact. It's generated because of additional dependency of LSI with BD. System takes care of cleaning the token for which this error is generated. This can be confirmed through VTY command show sandbox token.
DNS resolution for traceroute does not work for a router using the mgmt_vrf with 23.4R2-EVO.

On all Junos OS Evolved based platforms, when the RE (Routing Engine) node experiences switchover, offline/online transitions, or rebooting, a 'Sysman.re' crash file might appear in rare cases and could cause traffic impact.

On Junos Evolved PTX, AE (Aggregated Ethernet) re-anchoring is not working correctly when CFM (Connectivity Fault Management) is configured on untagged AE interfaces. Deleting an anchor child interface results in the associated CFM session going down. This can cause loss of CFM session continuity during AE re-anchoring operations involving untagged interfaces.
INLINEKA:CFM-SLM-RESPONDER No entry error might be seen with CFM configuration having more than one remote peer MEP in inline mode. There is no functional impact due to this error.

On Junos Evolved PTX platforms, a resource allocation error occurs when configuring inline CFM sessions at scales beyond the supported limits. This might cause session setup failures or unexpected behavior.

If the evo-aftmand-bt process restarts, the connection with the timingd process will get disconnected. The issue is that this does not get re-established resulting in the phy synchronization logic to fail in timingd after a few retries from its end. This might result in time error as the system is then no longer keeping the timestamp in the PHY/MAC in sync with the PTP FPGA.
On PTX10003 systems, it is not allowed to configure ZR optics (400G) through CLI.

On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) neighbourship configured with Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) authentication will go down during the Routing Engine (RE) switchover.
The cfmman process crashes with high scaled CFM configuration.
USB Media installation shows up minor alarm Host 0 Voltage Threshold Crossed.
The Netconf output for xml format shows ping-success tag under ping failure situation.
bt_mtip_chpcs_hw_clear_stats: failed error will be seen post rebooting the device.
Traffic is still forwarded after disabling ingress logical interface.
Traffic blackhole is observed for IPv4 /32 LDP prefixes advertised over BGP-LU when BGP sharding is configured.
Retimer/gearbox ports on LC1202 line card might take long duration to bring an interface back up.
Traffic going over LDP or LDPoRSVP route matching the CBF is getting impacted when PTX Junos OS Evolved platform working as PHP router with CBF configuration.
Traffic loss observed over load-balanced ESI LAG towards Provide Edge router in an EVPN-MPLS path on Junos OS Evolved PTX Series platforms.
Extend the interfaces optics-options configuration of DP init max duration for 400G ZR-M-HP optical transceiver.
FLT alpha algorithm gracefully rollback support.
MACSec statistics will not show up in the show interfaces intf-name statistics detail command output.
Router flag is not getting set in Neighbor Advertisement message.
[DCF14] [EVPN-VxLAN] After running a series of negative trigger tests on scale setup for 16 hours, traffic loss is seen in one IPv6 stream on PTX10001-36mr in CRB Spine and Border Router Role.
The rpd gets struck with 100% CPU usage after enabling BGP RIB-Sharding.
The evo-aftmand process crashes on PTX Junos OS Evolved platforms.
Chassis synchronization clock enters holdover state upon secondary BITS input failure.
Missing traffic statistics through telemetry on PTX Junos OS Evolved platforms with MPC10E, MPC11E, and LC9600 line cards.
Extra link flap will be seen when the link fails for a short time on PTX10000 with LC1202.
Route change is not synced after rpd restart due to rib-fib inconsistency.
The IPv6 firewall filter applied on loopback 0 Is not processing NS and NA packets.
EVPN next-hop installation for ESI over VTEP fails after remote device restart on PTX platforms.
PFH Interface Down After PFE Offline and Re-anchor.
SNMP walk failure due to missing OID after FCO/TPA delete compression.
The rpd crash due to overlapping flow route updates in a single transaction.
PPPoE over EVPN-MPLS tunnel does not work.
Control plane is not properly managing the label 1048575 for MPLS traffic, leading to service impact.
NPU's (Network Processing Unit) KHT (Kernal Hash Table) utilization shows 100% utilization post configuration commit.
Traffic drops will be observed when multiple interfaces are part of the same ASIC and configured with the same MAC address.
Wedge detected after multiple, rapid PFE restarts.
IS-IS adjacency between CE devices is not established over Layer 2 circuit.
Applying a Layer2 filter on interface on results in protocol flaps and traffic disruption on other interfaces on the same PFE.
PTX10002-36QDD showing incorrect power status.
Route installation for MPLS labels fails when an RSVP LSP goes down.
Rare assert with an Junos OS Evolved process.
Transient traffic loss during multicast route convergence scenarios.
Log messages getting disappeared after upgrade.
Display issue is observed for command output show forwarding-options port-mirroring self-mirror.
MACsec traffic impact due to incorrect port mapping.
Rare evo-cda-bt core in PTX10008 Junos OS Evolved with multiple FPCs, failure of one FPC triggers get-state, causing rapid offline of its PFEs.
PTX10000 Junos OS Evolved: JFLOW exported flow data InputInt is set to zero when redirecting to routing-instance and redirecting back to default instance.
The update of the parcel_dump script to support the new Aegon linecard.
JNP10K-LC1301 running on ASAN image will go into fault state after restart.
Mixing EP and SP style configurations on AE bundle causes traffic loss and protocol session failure on Junos OS Evolved PTX Series platforms.
LACP session destroy time is not getting updated in PFE.
Transit multicast traffic is getting blackhole due to peer interface flap.
Coredump during LAG disable.
Disabling a single AE IFL in a MAC-VRF can bring the entire AE interface down.
Interface remains administratively down state, fails to recover after execution of CLI command request interface bounce.
The eventd memory leak on Syslog over TLS with unconfigured PKI certificate
[PTX10000 Junos OS Evolved] Cold start SNMP trap is unexpectedly sent when doing primaryship switchover from RE1 to RE0, or backup RE reboot followed by primaryship switchover.
Process evo-aftmand-bt crashes on PTX10000 Junos OS Evolved platforms when command request chassis fpc slot pfe-instance restart is executed.
The firewalld process crashes post specific set of filter related modifications performed in single commit.
The changes from instance-type DEFAULT_INSTANCE to others and vice versa will not be allowed.
The advertise-inactive configuration does not work as expected when add-path multipath is configured and negotiated with the neighbor.
The MVPN traffic forwarding is affected when BGP PIC is enabled.

On Junos Evolved TD4 platform (QFX5130-48CM), intermittent link flaps causing the hardware link scan to malfunction, resulting in incorrect high values in the Correction Field (CF) of Precision Time Protocol (PTP) packets, causing improper timestamping. This impacts system time inaccuracies across the network and the overall timing synchronization of the network until remediated.

On the QFX5230/QFX5240 platforms, host injected control protocol frames are accounted under the egress port's best-effort queue ( Q0 by default) even though they are sent on the network control queue. this is only a display issue of the show command output and does not affect the actual prioritization of traffic.
This is unsupported configuration for channelized interfaces.
QFX5700 MacSec: Minor packet drops (0.0000001%) observed when MacSec is enabled.

USB disks with Junos OS Evolved images from Junos OS Evolved 23.4R2 onwards might not be detectable by Windows. They still have valid images, and can be used for Junos OS Evolved installs. The only issue is that new images cannot be installed on these USB disks because Windows no longer recognizes these USB drives.

On Junos Evolved platform QFX5230 and QFX5240, any type of interface flap will cause the Priority-based Flow Control (PFC) generation stops from the switch under storm condition after neighbor link flap.
Egress port speed field in the IFA 2.0 Metadata stack is not supported on QFX5230 and it is always '0' irrespective of the egress port. speed.

On QFX5000 Junos OS Evolved platforms interface counter sensor names are modified as per OpenConfig YANG model details. https://gnats.juniper.net/web/default/1860876/attachments/ interface_counter s_cvbc_details.docxPR1860876 On Junos Evolved OS platforms like QFX5000 (QFX5230/QFX5240), ungraceful swapping a 400G DAC with a 400G DR4 optic (or vice-versa) might lead to traffic loss.
Graceful JOJI of FPC is the recommended way instead of ungraceful.
There are only the logs seen related to getDieTemperature. There is no functionality effected and CPU is not effected. System is also stable.

On QFX5130 or QFX5700 platforms, in Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN (EVPN-VxLAN) scenario, the Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) Congestion Experienced (CE) bit is not be set for ECN-capable traffic when there is congestion. Since the CE bit is not set, packets are dropped.

On QFX5230-64CD platform, 400G DAC cable of 2.5m length and 4X100G DAC BO might not link up with some peer devices. This issue is not seen with all peer devices. If this happens, please replace the 2.5m cable with a 1m DAC cable or use supported 400G Optics instead.
Link with the DAC (SFP56-50G-DAC-3M ) comes up with 25G default speed configuration when switch is rebooted. Hence, When 50G speed config is applied, peer side sees the link flap.

Issue is not related to QFX5220 and not related to optics (QSFP56-DD-400GBASE-DR4) as mentioned in the PR synopsis and description. We encounter this issue is happening on the Marvel Line-side TX on the QFX5700. Input error and framing are small in number it should not have significant impact on traffic.

Junk values are shown for Carrier transition counter sometimes on initiating clear interfaces statistics all command and picd app restart. This issue is observed on QFX5220-32CD, QFX5230-64CD, QFX5240-64OD.
To ensure proper functionality of hitless restart/ISSU, do not mark any port as "unused".

When a VXLAN encapsulated IP packet, or an IP packet with UDP port matching the VXLAN UDP port, is received on a trunk interface that does not have VXLAN configuration it is dropped. The Issue is not seen with untagged L3 interfaces
DHCPv4/v6 packets may be dropped because DHCP packets are not routed to kernel after initial jdhcpd starts
In high-scale, high-load environments, the l2ald process may experience hangs during Apstra polling.
Packets are incorrectly directed to an inappropriate filter and are lost due to TCAM exhaustion.

VXLAN packets with inner VLAN tag are dropped in transit device.
OSPFv3 authentication with IPSEC doesn't work on Junos OS Evolved QFX platforms.
Traffic forwarding fails to recover after manually removing and reinserting the Direct Attached Copper cable.
ECN copy support from VXLAN header to inner Header on Type-5 decap tunnels.
The command output for show system snapshot randomly returns Error: Snapshot is in progress... Please retry later!
QFX5241-64OD: Media type not displayed correctly for OSFP DAC and DACBO cables.
Rare assert with an Junos OS Evolved process.
EVACL does not work on TH4 and TH5 when bound on access ports.
Optics description is displayed as UNKNOWN for 3PO optics on Junos OS Evolved platforms.
Duplicate traffic will occur in an EVPN-VxLAN DCI configuration with translation VNI.
